caption:
Fireflies is free to start, but the free plan has three real limits: 400 minutes of storage, 20 AI credits and a 2 hour cap per recording.
Pro is $10 a seat a month billed yearly, or $18 monthly.
The full breakdown, with AI credit prices, is on neurafeedai.com.

paragraphs.text: Fireflies AI pricing starts at zero. The Fireflies pricing page lists four plans: Free, Pro at $10 per seat a month billed yearly or $18 monthly, Business at $19 billed yearly or $29 monthly, and Enterprise at $39 per seat a month, sold yearly only. Paying yearly saves up to 44 percent, according to the page.

The free plan is useful on its own, but it has three limits that matter more than the price: how many minutes you can store, how many AI credits you get, and how long one recording can run. This guide goes through each, so you can tell when free stops being enough.
What the Fireflies free plan includes

On the free plan, Fireflies records meetings on Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams, and the Help Center adds Webex and other supported platforms. It transcribes in more than 100 languages with automatic language detection, lets you edit transcripts, and includes global search, a mobile app for in person meetings and a Chrome extension that records without adding a bot.
You can also upload audio and video files. The Help Center lists MP3, MP4, WAV and M4A files of up to 100MB and 150 minutes each, and says each upload uses one transcription credit.

Fireflies' own pages do not describe transcription on the free plan the same way. The pricing page and the Fireflies pricing blog say unlimited transcription. The Help Center says 3 meeting transcriptions are included by default, and that turning on Auto Join unlocks unlimited transcriptions for supported meetings and recordings.
The three free plan limits

Storage: the free plan holds 400 minutes of recordings, uploads and calls. The pricing page and the blog say 400 minutes per team, while the Help Center says per seat. The Fireflies blog says that once you hit the cap, you cannot view new meetings until you delete older ones.
AI credits: the free plan comes with 20 one-time AI credits. Fireflies says these sign-up credits do not expire. Pro also starts with 20, Business with 30 and Enterprise with 50.
Recording length: one free recording can run up to 2 hours. Pro has the same 2 hour limit, Business allows 3 hours and Enterprise 4 hours.

The free plan also leaves things out. According to the Fireflies blog, Free does not include video recording, AI Skills, the Personal Assistant, Voice Agents or downloads, so you cannot export transcripts or summaries.
How Fireflies AI credits work

Transcription does not cost AI credits. Fireflies says credits pay only for advanced features, such as AI Skills, Magic soundbites, custom summary sections, Voice Agents, Sales Assist, the Slack Assistant, CRM autofill and the Personal Assistant. Credits are charged per query with dynamic pricing, and reprocessing a summary is free.

If you run out, Fireflies sells monthly credit subscriptions. They start at $5 a month for 50 credits and go up to $600 a month for 10,000 credits, with 20 percent off when paid yearly. Purchased credits that you do not use do not carry over to the next month.
What Pro and Business add

Pro raises storage to 8,000 minutes per seat and adds video recording, downloads of transcripts, summaries and recordings, and unlimited integrations. Business removes the storage cap and adds a 3 hour recording limit, a multi-language mode, conversation intelligence and user groups. Enterprise adds SSO and SCIM, audit logs, custom retention and a HIPAA-ready setup with a BAA.

Third-party reviews describe the AI credits as the tightest part of every plan. ClickUp's review, updated in November 2026, calls the credits very restrictive for heavy users of the AI assistant, because even paid plans start with only 20 or 30.
How to check what you are using

paragraphs.title: 1. Start on Free and record a normal week
paragraphs.text: Connect your calendar, let Fireflies join the meetings you would normally record, and use it for one week before paying for anything.

paragraphs.title: 2. Count your recorded minutes
paragraphs.text: Add up how many minutes you recorded that week. At 400 minutes of storage, the free plan holds a little under seven one-hour calls in total, so a weekly total above that means you will start deleting meetings.

paragraphs.title: 3. Notice which AI features you reach for
paragraphs.text: If you only read transcripts and summaries, credits barely matter. If you keep asking for AI Skills or custom summary sections, your 20 credits will go fast.

paragraphs.title: 4. Check your longest meeting
paragraphs.text: If any of your calls run past 2 hours, neither Free nor Pro will capture the whole thing, and Business is the first plan with a longer limit.
Before you pay monthly, compare the yearly price. Pro drops from $18 to $10 a seat a month when billed yearly, about the 44 percent saving Fireflies advertises.

For most people, storage is the limit that ends the free plan, not transcription or credits. Anyone with more than a few recorded calls a week will either delete old meetings or move to Pro. People who mainly want searchable transcripts can stay on Free longer; people who want the AI extras should budget for credits as well as a plan.
Fireflies' own pages disagree on a few free plan details, such as whether storage is per team or per seat. Check the numbers in your own account settings before you plan around them.
